title: Chapter 53: Supreme Courage 3
content:
Chapter 53

Supreme Courage 3

The "rock island" cut through the dark water, surging straight toward the shore.

A suffocating pressure rolled off the approaching monstrosity, driving everyone back in frantic retreat. Only a handful stood their ground—Lan Wangji, Jin Zixuan, Jiang Cheng, and Wen Zhuliu. But right when everyone braced for whatever lurked beneath to violently breach the surface, it abruptly ground to a halt.

Landing on its back had startled the sleeping beast awake. Knowing one wrong move could trigger a slaughter, Wei Wuxian froze, waiting it out.

A few blood-red maple leaves drifted lazily across the pitch-black ripples encircling the rocky mound.

Deep beneath those leaves, down in the lightless belly of the pool, a pair of enormous shapes gleamed like polished brass mirrors.

The golden reflections expanded, rising fast. Shit, Wei Wuxian cursed inwardly. Hauling Wen Chao along, he took two measured steps back. Beneath their boots, the island heaved violently upward into empty air. Breaching the surface, an enormous, soot-black beast burst through the water, hoisting those stray maple leaves on its crown.

Through a chorus of panicked shrieks, the beast craned its neck with agonizing slowness, fixing a pair of wheel-sized eyes directly onto the two uninvited guests perched on its shell.

The rounded head looked bizarre—part tortoise, part viper. Taken alone, the head looked identical to a giant python's, but the body hauling itself out of the depths was shaped unmistakably like...

"Holy hell," Wei Wuxian muttered under his breath. "...That's one massive bastard of a turtle..."

And it was no ordinary turtle.

Drop this thing onto the training grounds at Lotus Pier, and that shell alone would swallow the entire yard whole. Its blackened head was so thick it would take three burly men linking arms just to encircle it. Ordinary turtles certainly didn't sport an impossibly long, coiling serpentine neck lined with rows of jagged, yellowed fangs—nor did they possess four clawed, terrifyingly nimble beast legs.

Wei Wuxian locked eyes with the monster's glowing golden irises. Its pupils thinned into vertical slits, widening and narrowing in erratic beats as if its vision were drifting in and out of focus, unable to resolve what was standing on its back.

Seems this thing shares a snake's lousy eyesight, he reasoned. If we don't twitch, it might not even register us.

Suddenly, two pressurized geysers of vapor blasted from its cavernous nostrils.

Those stray maple leaves had settled near its snout; irritated by the tickle, it had simply blown them off. Wei Wuxian held his breath, rigid as a stone statue, but the sudden snort completely shattered Wen Chao's fraying nerves.

Knowing how bloodthirsty these primordial horrors were, Wen Chao assumed the blast meant it was lunging. Forgetting the cold steel pressed to his jugular, he thrashed in absolute hysteria, screeching toward the bank: "Save me! Save me, damn it! What are you standing around for, Wen Zhuliu?!"

Jiang Cheng gritted his teeth, hissing, "You absolute moron!"

Watching one of the two blobs on its back suddenly flail like an insect while shrieking like a banshee, the beast's predatory instincts flared. Its snake-like neck coiled back and snapped forward like a coiled spring, jaws parting wide to snap down on its own shell!

Wei Wuxian swung his arm back and launched Wen Chao’s sword like an arrow straight for the monster's vitals, aiming dead-center where the neck met the body.

Clang!

The black scales armored its flesh like forged plate iron. The steel struck with a shower of sparks and bounced cleanly off, plunging uselessly into the dark water. The beast blinked, momentarily distracted, its massive eyes tracking the glittering, slender bar of steel sinking into the deep. Seizing the window, Wei Wuxian hauled Wen Chao by the scruff, sprang off the shell, and landed on another jagged rock jutting from the pool. He prayed to the heavens, Please tell me this rock isn't another damn turtle!

"Behind you!" Jiang Cheng roared from the shore. "The Core-Melting Hand!"

Wei Wuxian whipped around just as a pair of massive palms bore down on him in eerie silence. Pure reflex took over: he threw a palm strike to meet the attack. The clash struck like a falling mountain—a suffocating, shadowy force ripping into his meridians, threatening to hollow out the spiritual energy right out of his arm. Wei Wuxian yanked his hand back on pure survival instinct. Seizing the opening, Wen Zhuliu snatched Wen Chao by the collar and vaulted back to the safety of the shore. Cursing under his breath, Wei Wuxian leapt after them, landing on the bank a second later.

The Wen clan disciples had already unslung their bows. Backing away from the shore, they loosed a furious hail of arrows. Steel tipped shafts rained against the beast’s dark scales and shell in a blinding tempest of sparks and clattering ricochets. It looked like a desperate, grand battle, but it was useless—not a single shaft pierced vital flesh. It was like trying to tickle a boulder. The massive reptilian head swayed lazily from side to side; beneath the armor plating, its hide was coarse as weathered bedrock, shrugging off the arrows without a scratch.

Right beside him, a gasping Wen disciple was fumbling with his quiver, struggling to draw his bow halfway. Running out of patience, Wei Wuxian ripped the weapon right out of the boy's hands and kicked him sprawling into the dirt. Spotting three feathered arrows left in the quiver, he nocked all three in a single pull, drawing the wood to its absolute breaking point as he took aim. The bowstring groaned against his ear, ready to sing—when an ear-splitting shriek tore through the ranks behind him.

The cry was thick with pure, unadulterated terror.

Wei Wuxian whipped his head around. Wang Lingjiao was barking orders at three of her personal enforcers. Two burly guards had pinned Mianmian’s arms behind her, wrenching her head back by the chin, while the third brandished a glowing iron brand, driving it straight toward the girl's face!

The branding iron was incandescent, sizzling with raw heat. Too far to intervene on foot, Wei Wuxian pivoted his bow on a dime and released the string.

Three arrows whistled through the dark in a lethal burst, striking all three enforcers dead-center. Without so much as a groan, the men collapsed backward into the dirt.

Yet before the bowstring finished humming, Wang Lingjiao lunged. Snatching the discarded iron from the ground, she tangled her fist in Mianmian’s hair and drove the searing iron straight down toward her eyes!

Her cultivation was garbage, but the strike was viciously fast and steeped in pure malice. If that iron landed, even if Mianmian didn't lose an eye, her face would be permanently disfigured. Even trapped in a life-or-death subterranean nightmare, this vile woman couldn't suppress her sick, petty urge to ruin an innocent girl!

The other disciples were scattered, eyes glued to the monster in the pool as they desperately nocked arrows; no one was close enough to step in. His hands were empty, and snatching another bow was out of the question. Running on pure instinct, Wei Wuxian vaulted forward, one hand striking Wang Lingjiao’s wrist to break her grip on Mianmian’s hair while his other palm slammed into her chest.

Taking the full brunt of the blow, Wang Lingjiao spat a mouthful of blood and flew backward.

Yet the searing tip of that iron brand drove flush into Wei Wuxian’s chest.

A nauseating reek of singed silk and scorched flesh filled the air, thick with the sickening smell of meat cooking through. Beneath his collarbone, right over his heart, an agonizing wave of blinding pain tore through his chest.

He clamped his teeth together until they threatened to splinter, but the sheer, blistering agony shattered his jaw open, tearing a ragged roar from his throat.

That desperate palm strike had packed enough force to send Wang Lingjiao skidding across the stone, vomiting blood as she broke into hysterical wailing. Jiang Cheng moved in with a lethal strike aimed at her crown, sending Wen Chao into a frantic screech: "Jiaojiao! Jiaojiao! Save her, damn you! Bring Jiaojiao back!"

Wen Zhuliu’s brow pinched. Without a word, he blurred forward, knocking Jiang Cheng back with a concussive sweep, scooped up the sobbing girl, and dumped her unceremoniously at Wen Chao’s boots. Clinging to Wen Chao's robes, she wailed through mouthfuls of blood. Jiang Cheng lunged back into the fray, his eyes wild and rimmed with crimson veins.

Taking in Jiang Cheng's murderous snarl, the mutinous fury boiling through the rest of the young masters, and the colossal beast whose front left claw was already hauling its bulk onto the rocky bank, Wen Chao’s spine finally snapped. Terror won out. He shrieked, "Fall back! Pull back right now!"

His men had been clinging by a thread, just waiting for the order to flee. The moment the command dropped, they drew their swords and took flight. Wei Wuxian had dumped Wen Chao’s blade into the lake, so the young master simply shoved an underling off his sword, hauled Wang Lingjiao onto the steel, and shot toward the ceiling like a frightened bolt. The Wen enforcers scrambled after him like scattered roaches.

Jin Zixuan barked, "Hold your fire! Retreat!"

None of the disciples had any desire to keep brawling against a living mountain. Breaking into a dead sprint, they tore back down the tunnels toward the vertical drop—only to find the thick creeper vines they had used to climb down severed, coiled dead on the cavern floor like a pile of slaughtered snakes.

Jin Zixuan roared in fury, "Cowardly bastards! They cut the vines!"

Without those sturdy vines, scaling three hundred feet of sheer, slick subterranean rock was impossible. High above their heads, the circular mouth of the cave glowed with blinding white daylight. But within heartbeats, that circle of sky began to vanish, choked out like a lunar eclipse.

Someone screamed in panic, "They’re sealing the hole!"

Before the words fully landed, the remaining sliver of light was snuffed out.

Pitch darkness rushed in, broken only by the flickering glow of a few dying torches, casting long, wavering shadows across a circle of pale, bewildered faces. Dead silence settled over the abyss.

Finally, Jin Zixuan’s venomous curse shattered the hush: "Those shameless, rotting dogs really went through with it!"

A disciple murmured weakly, "It's fine... My clan will come for us. Once my parents hear about this, they'll track us down..."

A few uncertain voices chimed in, but someone cut through the delusion with a trembling rasp: "They think we're in Qishan attending 're-education'! Why would they come looking for us here?! When the Wen Clan gets back, they'll spin a lie to cover their tracks... We're trapped down here..."

"We're buried alive... No rations... locked in the dark with that monster..."

Footsteps shuffled over as Jiang Cheng approached, half-carrying Wei Wuxian by the shoulder. Hearing the panic about food, Wei Wuxian managed a strained drawl: "Hey Jiang Cheng... there's a fresh cut of roasted meat right here. Hungry?"

"Shut your damn mouth!" Jiang Cheng snapped. "That iron didn't burn your tongue off, did it? Look at the mess we're in—I ought to sew those lips together."

Lan Wangji’s pale gaze lingered on them for a beat before shifting toward Mianmian, who was hovering behind them in tears. Her face was a ruin of snot and sobbing, fingers twisting her skirt into knots as an endless stream of "I'm sorry, I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry" tumbled from her lips.

Wei Wuxian pressed a palm to his ear, groaning, "Can you stop crying? I’m the one who took the hit, not you. What, do you want me to comfort you now? How about you comfort me instead? Alright Jiang Cheng, ease off—my legs aren't broken."

A few other maidens crowded around Mianmian, their quiet sniffling filling the gloom.

Lan Wangji withdrew his stare, turning on his heel to walk back down the tunnel.

Jiang Cheng called out, "Second Young Master Lan, where are you going? That monster is still guarding the pool."

"Back to the water," Lan Wangji answered quietly. "There is a way out."

The promise of an exit choked the sobs off instantly. Wei Wuxian asked, "What do you mean?"

Lan Wangji said, "The pool holds maple leaves."

To anyone else, the answer sounded absurd, but the spark ignited in Wei Wuxian’s head immediately.

Back in that dark subterranean pool, a few crimson maple leaves had indeed drifted across the surface. Yet there were no maples inside this cavern, no human trails, and only an ancient banyan choked the mouth of the fissure above. Those leaves had been crisp, fresh, and brilliant red. When they had hiked up Mount Muxi earlier, they had crossed a mountain stream carrying those exact same fallen leaves.

Realization dawned on Jiang Cheng as well: "There must be an underwater fissure at the bottom of that pool connecting to an outside stream. The current washed those leaves in!"

A disciple piped up, voice shaking with doubt: "B-but... how do we know the gap is large enough to squeeze through? What if it's too narrow? What if it's just a hairline crack in the bedrock?"

Jin Zixuan’s brow pinched. "And that beast is planted right in the water; it won't budge."

Wei Wuxian pulled his collar open, gently fanning the blistered, mangled burn beneath his robes. "A shred of hope beats rotting down here waiting for rescue. So what if it's guarding the pool? We just need to lure it out."

Half an incense stick later, the disciples crept back down the tunnel, peering into the cavern from the shadows.

The beast was still largely submerged in the black water. Its long, serpentine neck extended from the shell, nosing along the shore. Opening its yellowed fangs, it delicately clamped down on a stray Wen corpse, coiling its neck back to drag the meal into the shadowy safety of its shell, settling in to feast in peace.

Wei Wuxian hurled a lit torch through the air, sending it clattering against the rocky wall across the cave.

In the suffocating quiet, the sharp clatter hit like thunder. Instantly, the beast’s head snaked back out of its armor. Its slit pupils caught the dancing flame. Drawn by pure predatory instinct toward light and heat, its snout slowly drifted toward the fire.

Behind its blind spot, Jiang Cheng slipped silently into the black current.

Born and raised on the waterways of Yunmeng, the disciples of the Jiang Clan possessed peerless swimming skills. Jiang Cheng slid beneath the surface without splashing a single drop, leaving barely a ripple behind. The young masters held their breath, eyes darting between the water and the monster. The massive serpent head hovered near the torch, hesitating, inching closer and pulling back in agonizing uncertainty.

Finally, curiosity won out. It leaned its snout in to investigate—only for the searing heat of the flame to singe its scales.

Its head whipped back, snorting two furious blasts of steam that snuffed the torch out cold.

Right at that second, Jiang Cheng broke the surface, gasping for air. Sensing its domain invaded, the beast swung its neck around, fangs baring as it lunged toward him!

Shit! Wei Wuxian bit down hard on his thumb, quickly smearing several frantic talismans across his palm in blood. He bolted from the shadows and slammed his hand against the stone. The moment his palm cleared the dirt, a roaring wall of crimson flames surged higher than a man’s head!

Startled by the blaze, the beast wheeled back toward the shore. Scrambling out of the water, Jiang Cheng bellowed, "There's a tunnel down there! It's massive!"

Wei Wuxian shouted over the crackle of fire, "How massive?!"

"Wide enough for five or six people to swim through shoulder-to-shoulder!"

Wei Wuxian’s command cut through the cavern like steel: "Listen up! Stick to Jiang Cheng and get into the water! Uninjured disciples look after the wounded, strong swimmers guide the ones who can't swim! Five or six can pass at once, so don't you dare trample each other! Move! In the water, now!"

The blazing wall of flame sputtered out. Wei Wuxian retreated a dozen paces, slamming his bloody palm into the ground again to detonate a second eruption of earth-fire. The golden glare in the monster's eyes reflected the flames, whipping it into a frenzy. Digging its four massive clawed limbs into the stone, its mountain-sized bulk dragged itself onto the bank, lumbering straight toward him.

Jiang Cheng roared, "What the hell are you doing?!"

"What the hell does it look like?! Get them into the water!"

He had successfully lured the monster out of the pool—if they didn't run now, they never would! Jiang Cheng gritted his teeth, turning to the terrified crowd. "Everyone to me! Strong swimmers on the left, non-swimmers on the right!"

Wei Wuxian was methodically backstepping, calculating the terrain as he laid down bursts of flame to keep the monster hooked. Out of nowhere, a sharp, searing pain tore through his forearm. Glancing down, an arrow was jutting from his flesh.

That very same Lan disciple who had buckled under pressure earlier had snatched a discarded Wen bow, attempting to shoot the monster. Paralyzed by terror at its speed and ferocity, his trembling hands had slipped, sending the shaft whistling straight into Wei Wuxian's arm. With no time to pull the steel, Wei Wuxian slammed another burst of flame into the floor, snarling, "Fall back! Stop getting in my damn way!"

The disciple had only wanted to redeem himself by landing a vital blow; watching the arrow plunge into his savior instead, his face drained of color, and he threw himself into the water in frantic flight.

Jiang Cheng hollered from the shoreline, "Hurry up and get over here!"

"Right behind you!"

Jiang Cheng was shepherding three non-swimmers—the final batch. He couldn't afford to hesitate; biting his tongue, he dove beneath the surface to guide them through.

Wei Wuxian reached down and wrenched the arrow from his forearm. The second the shaft cleared the flesh, a cold realization struck him: Oh, no.

The scent of fresh, hot blood whipped the beast into an absolute frenzy. Its neck shot forward, jaws unhinging wide!

Before Wei Wuxian could react, a sudden concussive palm strike caught his ribs, shoving him clear of the strike.

Lan Wangji had shoved him aside.

The upper and lower jaws snapped shut like an iron maiden, crushing down on Lan Wangji’s right leg.

Just watching the impact made Wei Wuxian’s own leg throb with phantom agony. Yet Lan Wangji’s face remained an unyielding mask of stone, his brows pinching in a microscopic wince as he was dragged violently backward!

With the beast's monstrous jaw strength, snapping a grown man in half at the waist was child's play. By some miracle, it disliked mangled prey; once it clamped onto a victim, dead or alive, its instinct was to drag them whole into the armored sanctuary of its shell to feed at leisure. Had it exerted even an ounce of jaw pressure, Lan Wangji’s leg would have sheared off instantly. But that shell was an impenetrable fortress; once it pulled him inside, he was as good as dead!

Wei Wuxian tore forward in a dead sprint. Right before the beast’s head retracted beneath the rim of the shell, he threw himself through the air, his hands clamping onto a massive upper fang!

His mortal strength was nothing compared to this primordial horror, yet staring down a friend's death, a surge of monstrous adrenaline detonated through his veins. Planting both boots hard against the outer edge of the shell, he hung on to that fang with white-knuckled desperation, acting like a jammed wedge, refusing to let the jaws close, denying it its meal.

Lan Wangji looked up, stunned disbelief shattering his stoic mask—he hadn't expected Wei Wuxian to dive back into the jaws of death for him.

Terrified the monster would snap and either swallow them whole or bite Lan Wangji’s leg off, Wei Wuxian kept his right hand locked around the upper fang, jammed his left hand against the lower jaw, and wrenched in opposite directions with everything he had. Veins bulged along his neck and forehead until they looked ready to burst, his face flushed scarlet with raw exertion.

The fangs had buried deep into Lan Wangji’s flesh, yet under that impossible, suicidal leverage, the iron jaws slowly, agonizingly pried apart!

Losing its grip on its quarry, Lan Wangji dropped heavily into the pool. The moment he was clear, the divine surge of strength vanished from Wei Wuxian’s muscles. He could no longer hold the jaws; his hands slipped, and the rows of jagged yellow fangs slammed shut with an ear-splitting crash like grinding bedrock!

Wei Wuxian tumbled into the water, splashing down right beside Lan Wangji. Rolling in the dark current to right himself, he hooked an arm under Lan Wangji’s chest, kicked with his legs, and dragged him several yards across the pool in a clean, surging wake. Scrambling onto the shore, he hoisted Lan Wangji onto his back and bolted down the tunnel.

Lan Wangji rasped in shock, "You...?"

Wei Wuxian grinned through his panting breaths. "Yep, it's me! Surprised?"

Slumped over his back, Lan Wangji’s voice carried a rare, violent tremor: "Surprised by what?! Put me down!"

Even running for dear life, Wei Wuxian’s mouth refused to stay shut. "If I put you down just because you told me to, wouldn't that hurt my pride?"

Behind them, the beast's subterranean roar rattled the cavern, the concussive pressure slamming against their eardrums and rattling their lungs until the coppery tang of blood rose in their throats. Wei Wuxian clamped his mouth shut and focused on running. To keep the raging titan from crushing them, he deliberately wove through narrow, winding crevices where that massive shell couldn't fit. He ran without a single pause, on and on through the dark, until the roars faded into absolute silence.

Only then did his pounding footsteps slow.

The second the adrenaline receded, a thick, metallic stench of fresh blood filled the air. Reaching behind him, his right hand came away drenched in warm, slick crimson.

Wei Wuxian's heart sank into his stomach. Shit. Lan Zhan's leg just got a hundred times worse.
